q: Until what post-conceptional age are ex-premature babies at increased risk of post-op apnoea?
why: Need apnoea monitoring and an inpatient bed if under 60 weeks PCA.

q: Which factor worsens apnoea risk in ex-prems?
why: Also hypoxia, hypothermia, hypoglycaemia, sepsis and opioids; caffeine reduces risk.

q: What did the GAS trial find?
o: No difference in neurodevelopment at 2 years or IQ at 5 years between awake regional and under 1 hour of sevoflurane
It was stopped early for harm
why: Infants under 60 weeks PMA having hernia repair.

q: What did the MASK study find with multiple exposures before age 3?
o: Small reductions in processing speed and fine motor skills, and more parent-reported behaviour problems
why: Single exposure showed no difference in IQ.

q: What did the 2016 FDA warning concern?
o: Repeated or lengthy (over 3 h) GA in children under 3 or pregnant women in the third trimester
why: This prompted the human studies that followed.

q: What is the approximate blood volume of a neonate?
why: Around 90 ml/kg with HbF 80% at birth.

q: Why are neonates prone to hypothermia?
o: High BSA:volume ratio and no shivering
why: They rely on brown fat (non-shivering thermogenesis), which is reduced in prems.

q: What is the APRICOT in-hospital mortality rate?
why: Severe critical incidents occurred in about 1 in 20 anaesthetics.

q: Why is cardiac output heart-rate dependent in neonates?
Which regional techniques are used for ex-prem hernia repair?
why: Awake spinal or caudal is an option; regional suits unilateral repair.
